assessments.strengths: The eleven points give a coherent account centered on immutable revisions and shared canvas commands. Tree-to-canvas continuity is clear: the editor preserves its seven responsibility branches while reducing the central tree from 103 to 71 lines. Peripheral expansions distinguish gesture settlement, selection, routing, and persistence.
assessments.weaknesses: Agent Chat and Generation combines several substantial responsibilities, while static analysis has no selected point. Most connections explain peripheral expansions rather than show interactions between them. The API overview remains lengthy at 101 lines.
assessments.improvementPotential: Separate conversation orchestration from validated generation within the overview, simplify API route detail, and connect gesture settlement, state publication, and persistence directly. These are tractable improvements to an already coherent core.

assessments.strengths: Explicit modular, call, ownership, and data-dependency perspectives clarify distinctions that A1 sometimes leaves implicit. The generation canvas distinguishes direct chat submission from generator-backed editing. Specific anchors connect central concepts to retry, validation, and lifecycle details.
assessments.weaknesses: The broader perspectives also repeat information: central generation, evaluation, and canvas-command trees remain 107, 108, and 102 lines. Every canvas edge touches the central diagram, leaving relationships among peripheral responsibilities embedded in prose. Generation remains a broad combined point.
assessments.improvementPotential: Consolidate repeated owners and inputs, shorten the central trees, and replace selected explanatory spokes with explicit operational connections. The opportunity is substantial, but it requires more restructuring than A1 and retains the same narrower point coverage.

assessments.strengths: Thirteen points balance the shared core with separate chat, validated generation, and static-analysis responsibilities. The analysis canvas usefully distinguishes CLI extraction from pinned diagram-range joins and concept partitions. Workflow-oriented hierarchies remain recognizable from the seeds; the evaluation central tree is comparatively manageable at 62 lines.
assessments.weaknesses: Runtime composition still leans toward a file-and-route inventory, with deployment switches and request details competing with service boundaries. All canvas connections involve the central diagram, so useful dependencies between peripheral panels remain textual.
assessments.improvementPotential: Reorganize runtime composition around responsibilities and resource ownership, then connect capture, generation, acknowledgement, and publication across panels. A strong alternative, but its workflow-oriented approach overlaps more with C1 than B2 does.

assessments.strengths: The thirteen-point selection combines useful subsystem coverage with explicit architectural perspectives. The editor preserves its modular, ownership, call, and dependency branches from tree to canvas. Persistence distinguishes workspace-manifest publication from catalog publication, while generation separates preparation, installation, and acknowledgement. Static analysis includes the useful diagram-leaf-to-concept-group boundary.
assessments.weaknesses: The same components recur across perspectives, and the persistence central tree still spans 98 lines with detailed thresholds, retry timings, and storage mechanics. Connections remain central-to-peripheral expansions rather than a visible network of collaborating responsibilities.
assessments.improvementPotential: High: retain the architectural distinctions while giving shared entities one concise description, moving parameter-level details outward, and adding meaningful connections between existing panels. Persistence and editor canvases offer concrete opportunities to improve readability without changing the selected points.

assessments.strengths: The fifteen points make useful separations between revisions and parsing, workspace ownership and native rendering, and validated generation and chat. The rendering overview contracts from 88 to 56 lines while retaining projection, settlement, history, and cleanup. Workspace edges explicitly connect session commits to record projection and then delivery, giving the canvas operational connectivity beyond expansion spokes.
assessments.weaknesses: Composition, canvas commands, and evaluation still have central trees of 99, 92, and 96 lines. Fine details such as camera defaults and shape dimensions compete with architectural explanations in peripherals. Splitting responsibilities across more points also creates repeated boundary descriptions.
assessments.improvementPotential: High: compress the three dense overviews, remove repeated boundary explanations, and extend the workspace canvas's meaningful connectivity to rendering and generation. The point selection and readable workflow hierarchy provide a strong foundation for focused refinement.

assessments.strengths: It retains C1's useful responsibility boundaries and adds explicit ownership and dependency perspectives. Workspace connections show optimistic-cache updates and editor remounts; the chat canvas connects captured history to isolated child controllers. The static-analysis canvas distinguishes analyzer execution from the static calls represented in its results.
assessments.weaknesses: Several overviews become substantially denser than C1: agent access reaches 108 lines, source evidence 103, and chat 104. Repeated perspective headings and detailed lifecycle descriptions make central and peripheral content harder to distinguish. The extra text does not consistently produce more meaningful connectivity.
assessments.improvementPotential: Compress repeated owners, inputs, and lifecycle steps while preserving the useful cross-panel links. Improvements are feasible, but selecting it alongside C1 would fund the same point selection twice, with much of the work devoted to reducing density.

rationale: C1 offers strong responsibility boundaries, readable workflow continuity, and concrete operational edges such as session commit -> record projection -> delivery. B2 complements it with explicit architectural perspectives and useful distinctions around publication, acknowledgement, and source-to-concept joins. Its repetition and central-tree density provide clear, tractable improvement targets. B1 is a strong runner-up but resembles C1's workflow-oriented approach; C2 duplicates C1's selected points with heavier overviews. Neither selection depends on output size. No dominant toy-example overfitting is apparent; repeated perspective and peripheral-expansion templates are the more evident risk. This assessment uses only the supplied selected points, trees, canvas text, positions, and edges; source-grounding claims inside those outputs were not independently verified.
